_comment: Same test as text_rebase_t5base_t5large_theseus_hubcheckpoint.json / text_rebase_t5base_t5large_steer_hubcheckpoint.json, but method=bico and B=google/flan-t5-large instead of the raw t5-v1_1-large -- flan-t5-large is what made steer_text's Stage 2 work (its instruction-tuned pretraining gives its own pooled features actual class structure, unlike raw t5-v1_1-large). bico shares theseus's TextEncoderShim/activation-hook machinery (rebase/text/adapters.py) and the same name-exact block matching, so it inherits the same depth-mismatch caveat theseus has: only the first 12 of B's 24 blocks receive any transported signal, the rest stay at B's pretrained/instruction-tuned weights untouched. Unlike theseus, bico drives its forward through an injected gradient recipe (seq_classification_recipe), pairing input activations with output gradients rather than pure input/output covariance.
_source_base_UNVERIFIED: source_model_name_or_path is google-t5/t5-base (original T5, not t5-v1_1-base) because varun-v-rao/t5-base-snli's model name implies that base -- confirmed by its own model card's training/eval description elsewhere in this conversation, but re-check if you swap the checkpoint.
_source_input_template: varun-v-rao/t5-base-snli expects a single formatted string, not this repo's default tokenizer(premise, hypothesis) pair encoding -- confirmed with scripts/probe_nli_input_format.py (pair encoding: ~0.35 accuracy / chance; this template: ~0.91, matching the model card's claimed 0.8982). A-only: B still uses the default pair encoding.
_target_head_note: target_task_heads must point to a nearest-mean-cosine head built FOR flan-t5-large specifically (scripts/build_nearest_mean_head.py --model-name-or-path google/flan-t5-large ...) -- the head built earlier for t5-v1_1-large will NOT work here (wrong backbone, wrong feature space).
